question: Poles were shocked to learn that the mObywatel application may be discontinued. The announced amendment to the Act on Trust Services and Electronic Identification is aimed at implementing the provisions of the eIDAS 2.0 Regulation and launching the European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet) application in Poland – a tool that allows EU residents to prove their identity and store various digital documents.

A similar application already exists in Poland – the aforementioned mObywatel, which has over 11 million users. It allows users to store documents, including their ID cards, driving licences, licences to exercise specific professions, and student or pensioner ID cards. Although the amendment to the Act and the implementation of eIDAS 2.
0 do not automatically mean that the mObywatel application will be discontinued, many doubts have been raised about the possibility of both ecosystems functioning in parallel. 1.

Was the Commission aware of the successful operation of the mObywatel application during work on the eIDAS 2.0 Regulation, and if so, was the possibility of integrating the EUDI Wallet with analogous national solutions examined?
Does the Commission recommend maintaining a single digital identity wallet per Member State, or does it permit the coexistence of two parallel, potentially competing solutions?

In the Commission’s opinion, does mObywatel meet the requirements of eIDAS 2.0, and is it possible to integrate both ecosystems within the existing mObywatel application? If so, does the Commission plan to encourage national authorities to ensure interoperability between them?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.4.2026) The Commission fully supports the successful operation of the mObywatel application. Poland is constructively cooperating with the Commission and is efficiently implementing a comprehensive development plan managed by the Ministry of Digital Affairs, positioning itself as one of the frontrunners in the development of European Digital Identity Wallets.

Under the European Digital Identity Regulation1, Member States are required to provide European Digital Identity Wallets by December 2026. The Commission has been informed that Poland is preparing a new version of mObywatel application, which will comply with the requirements for the European Digital Identity Wallets.

According to the information received, the European Digital Identity Wallet will constitute an additional component of the mObywatel application ecosystem. All documents used in mObywatel will stay accessible to the users. Existing national eID solutions and the European Digital Identity Wallets may continue to coexist.

Poland is actively participating in the European pilot projects POTENTIAL2 and APTITUDE3 supporting the development and testing of digital identity wallets. The experience gained contributes to the design of the Polish implementation of the European Digital Identity Wallet.

The Commission cooperates with Member States through these projects and the broader implementation process to ensure that European Digital Identity Wallets meet legal requirements and function across the EU.
1 Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 July 2014 on electronic

identification and trust services for electronic transactions in the internal market and repealing Directive 1999/93/EC, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32014R0910. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/digital-buildingblocks/sites/spaces/EUDIGITALIDENTITYWALLET/pages/924976339/LSP-POTENTIAL. 3 https://aptitude.digital-identity-wallet.eu/.
